body:
# Independent audit: attained critical-cap reciprocal-exit selection



Source: `candidate f27e81791899727a`.


fixed-source-trace scope.** This is a selection and exact optimization
theorem, not a dimension/parity bound on the selected correction and not
a proof of OC.

## 1. Closed projected menu

The cap mass is a finite sum of continuous one-dimensional tail functions
of a.(z-p), because the continuous normal u is nonzero and all measured
fibers have positive d-volume. After a subsequence every such parameter
has a limit in the compact extended line. Infinite limits can be replaced
by uniform finite full/empty saturation bounds. The projection of the
remaining polyhedron A intersected with these bounds is closed, so the
finite limits and the desired E-projection have a common finite lift.
That lift has exactly the limiting cap mass Q. This argument remains
valid with arbitrary extra fixed closed polyhedral constraints in A.
It does not use the false closed-projection principle for general closed
sets. Fibers omitted from P have zero relevant d-volume and make no
contribution to the continuity argument.

## 2. Exact exit formula and convexity

The lower section support m(z)=min u.x is finite and convex on the row
hull B, lower semicontinuous by compactness, and continuous on each
closed segment from p to a destination. The source reserve
delta=c-m(p)>0 gives a relative neighborhood of p in every K_b, by
mixing a strictly feasible source point with finitely many destination
points. Thus every exit fraction is strictly positive.

For h_j(s)=s[c-m(p+d_j/s)], convex perspective gives concavity, and the
direct interpolation calculation gives

    h_j(s_2)-h_j(s_1)>=delta(s_2-s_1).

The exact membership equivalence is

    p+d_j/s in K_b iff b.d_j<=h_j(s),   s>=1.

It proves the clipped inverse formula, not just an estimate. Its epigraph
is a convex set, so s_j=1/t_j is finite continuous convex. The same slope
bound controls its Lipschitz constant and all endpoint inverse slopes.

## 3. Attainment and the secondary choice

Positive barycentric row weights and spanning of E imply that every
nonzero b has some b.d_j>0. Compactness of the unit sphere yields the
strict uniform eta in the source. With
L=c-min_{C restricted to B}u.x>0, h_j(s)<=Ls proves coercivity of
sum theta_j/t_j, including when a term is clipped at one.

The feasible projected menu is nonempty and closed, hence the coercive
continuous objective attains its minimum and its minimizer set is
compact. No convexity of that set was used.

For Hausdorff continuity of K_b, a limiting feasible pair is retained by
compactness; conversely mixing any feasible pair with the fixed strictly
feasible source produces a strict pair valid for nearby b. Compactness
upgrades this pointwise approximation to Hausdorff convergence. Every
K_b has full E-dimension, so its E-volume is continuous. The secondary
maximum is therefore attained. A proper convex inclusion strictly
increases E-volume and cannot coexist with equal minimal reciprocal
cost. This proves precisely the stated inclusion maximality, without
asserting a dominating cap. The minimum-norm finite lift is attained
because its critical fiber is closed and squared norm is coercive.

## 4. Derivatives and the polyhedral case

The inverse of an increasing concave function has subgradient interval
[1/h'_-,1/h'_+]. At the clipping level it is [0,1/h'_+(1)], including a
possible infinite right slope. Positive lower slope delta prevents an
undefined reciprocal. The sum rule and directional derivative formula
apply to finite convex functions. Local Lipschitz continuity controls
the o(epsilon) remainder of a feasible one-sided curve in the possibly
nonconvex menu. Thus (15) is a valid necessary condition, not an
unjustified convex normal-cone assertion about that menu.

For polytopal C, m(p+t d_j)=max_l(alpha_l+beta_l t) on [0,1]. Each
alpha_l<=m(p)<c, so every denominator in the source's formula (16) is
strictly positive. Solving all inequalities
s(c-alpha_l)>=b.d_j+beta_l proves the exact maximum-of-affines formula.

## 5. Original residual optimizer and KKT data

At lambda_z>0, complementary slackness originally says the obstacle
equals h_z, so ebar_z>=h_z. The proposed inequalities force the new
minimum obstacle to equal h_z: if ebar_z=h_z the lower bound suffices;
if ebar_z>h_z both bounds make the new cap residual equal h_z. At a
zero-multiplier base the new obstacle remains at most h_z. Therefore
primal feasibility and every obstacle complementary-slackness equation
survive, while the objective gradient, slope constraints, and all other
stationarity equations are literally unchanged. The original optimizer,
multipliers, and the previously defined coupling can consequently be
retained.

For fixed nonzero u, residual section volume is a continuous monotone
function of the one integer-normal parameter. Every strict interior
volume level has a unique threshold because each interior slab of a
full-dimensional convex fiber has positive volume. Endpoint level sets
are closed half-lines or whole/empty sets. Hence all these requirements
are indeed finite closed polyhedral constraints, and the old cap makes
them feasible. Fixed source trace preserves its original cap incidence.

## 6. Actual cover preservation

This conclusion correctly uses extra fixed-witness circuit assumptions,
not residual primal feasibility. A cap through a deepest point in a
positive fiber has a proper own section. If it had positive margin at
another deepest point, a small threshold increase would retain that
point and lose positive own-fiber slab mass, contradicting raw depth Q.
Thus every selected cap has nonpositive margin at all deepest points.

The unchanged positive continuous-normal balance makes each circuit's
weighted margin purely affine in the integer base. It is nonpositive on
the convex hull of deepest bases and zero at its witness, so vanishes on
the witness's minimal face. Above that whole real face, its weighted cap
margin is zero for every continuous point; some closed cap contains the
point. Retaining the original slack covers handles nondeepest fibers.
Multiple witness anchor equations for a shared cap are compatible
because the original parameter satisfies them. This proves exactly the
claimed cover preservation.

## 7. Limits of the conclusion

The theorem selects one genuinely critical cap with finite minimal exit
cost and an inclusion-maximal residual projection. It does not bound
that cost by dimension, parity, or the conjectured depth, and does not
make all minima coordinatewise dominating. Those limitations are stated
explicitly and preserved throughout the proof. No correction to the
source was needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
